cases.setup: Provide a pinned public Python analyzer checkout with doctest setup, binding collision logic, and doctest tests; do not prebind historical paths.
checks: Recorded owner bindings include current code anchors for the initializer, collision handler, and test owner.
The probe records whether module underscore and source-less synthetic insertion share the reported collision mechanism.
The adapted reproduction has an observed result rather than an assumed historical traceback.
The checkout content remains unchanged.

cases.setup: Supply the baseline-reviewed initializer PortValue and observed applicability with a confirmed module scope.
checks: The resulting diff conditions synthetic underscore insertion on absence from the confirmed module scope.
The synthetic insertion remains present on the no-module-underscore branch.
General parent traversal and unrelated binding handling are unchanged.
The initializer output has conditionally-guarded state and stale validation observations are invalidated.
The public validate Action remains in the verification closure.

cases.setup: Supply a baseline-reviewed public doctest test owner with a confirmed doctest-enabled analyzer harness.
checks: The added source includes a module import aliased to underscore and a function with a pass-only doctest.
The assertion explicitly requires the ordinary unused-import diagnostic.
Existing doctest assertions remain present.
The tests output has collision-regression-added state.
The test addition is not represented as an observed passing execution.

cases.setup: Supply guarded initializer and regression-added test PortValues, with public current argv bindings for all three Oracles.
checks: The rendered public reproduction command completes without the source-less binding AttributeError.
The added regression executes and reports the expected unused-import diagnostic.
Adjacent public doctest checks execute, including an observed no-module-underscore path or an explicitly reported coverage gap.
The report records actual commands, outcomes, and semantic Oracle check states.
An unbound or failed Oracle prevents recording the required passed effect.
The report does not claim whole-project or cross-project validation from changed-file checks.
